svg.title: The size of the New Jerusalem on today's map
svg.desc: A map of the eastern Mediterranean and Middle East with a gold square 12,000 stadia (about 2,220 km) on each side centred on present-day Jerusalem. It reaches from Athens and Istanbul in the north-west to Ur in the south-east, and takes in Patmos, Ephesus, Cairo, Damascus, Nineveh, Babylon and Medina. Below, a side view shows the city's height of about 2,220 km against the curve of the earth, five times the height at which the International Space Station orbits.
svg.text: 12,000 stadia each way (Revelation 21:16), set over today’s map for size
SIDE VIEW · HEIGHT AGAINST THE CURVE OF THE EARTH

g.text: International Space Station orbit, about 420 km
the ground: a jet flies at 11 km, Everest stands 8.8 km, both inside this line
Scripture names the city Jerusalem and brings it down to the new earth (21:2, 10) without placing it on a map. Centring it on
today’s Jerusalem shows its size only; the first earth “passed away” and “the sea was no more” (21:1), so today’s coasts may not carry over.
For comparison, 2,220 km is a little more than Perth to Adelaide (about 2,130 km). Map: azimuthal equidistant projection centred on
Jerusalem, so distances from the centre are true. Coastlines from Natural Earth (public domain).
